quiz: The slot adds a layer of indirection. Think about what can change inside the page without breaking index entries.

Redo repeats history so the database returns to its exact state at the crash; undo comes after.
With no-force, data pages are written later, so durability at commit comes from the log alone.
SSTables are immutable, so a delete must be written as something new rather than erased in place.
Compare how often each strategy rewrites data against how many sorted runs it leaves to read and store.
Multiply the first level size by the fanout repeatedly until a level holds at least one terabyte.

Compare inserts that append at the right edge of the tree with inserts scattered across random leaves.
Think about per-block statistics that let the engine skip blocks whose value range cannot match.
In WAL mode new page versions go to the -wal file. Think about how they get back into the main file.
